headline: Sales and profit beat guidance, pushing a raised outlook
summary_short: Church & Dwight's Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 1.6% y/y to $1.53 billion -- ahead of its own outlook -- with organic sales up 5.8% and diluted EPS of $0.85, up from $0.78 a year ago.
summary_long: Net sales rose 1.6% y/y to $1,530.0 million, beating the company's guided ~1% decline, as organic sales grew 5.8% (Domestic +5.1%, International +9.1%, Specialty +2.8%) on volume growth and favorable price/mix, plus the MISS MOUTH'S acquisition. Gross margin expanded 240bp to 45.4% on volume, productivity, and acquisition mix, partly offset by inflation and transportation costs. Operating income rose 5.6% to $276.4 million despite higher marketing (+$8.2M) and SG&A, including Touchland restricted-stock charges; diluted EPS was $0.85, up from $0.78. Cash fell to $254.8 million from $923.2 million a year ago, mainly reflecting the $300 million MISS MOUTH'S acquisition. Church & Dwight raised full-year guidance for net sales, organic growth, adjusted EPS, and cash flow to ~$1.175 billion.

drivers.explanation: Net sales beat the company's guided ~1% decline as organic sales growth accelerated to 5.8% on 4.3% volume growth and 1.5% favorable price/mix, plus the MISS MOUTH'S acquisition.
Gross-margin expansion (+240bp) was partly offset by higher marketing spend (+$8.2M) and higher SG&A, including Touchland-related restricted-stock charges.
Growth reflects the operating-income increase and a lower effective tax rate (20.3% vs 23.8% last year), partly offset by higher other expense from lower interest income.
Cash fell from a year ago primarily due to the $300 million MISS MOUTH'S acquisition and other acquisition/financing outflows in the trailing six months.
The company raised FY2026 guidance for net sales, organic growth, adjusted EPS, and cash from operations, citing stronger-than-expected first-half growth and confidence in second-half momentum.
